symbols.name: \(v\)
symbols.def: Index selecting the lower- or upper-endpoint gap profile.

symbols.name: \(r\)
symbols.def: Number of exact-tie cells in the explicit high-information profile slice.

symbols.name: \(d\)
symbols.def: Positive factor used only by the pushforward family in \(\mathrm{def:scaled-pushforward-experiment}\); it does not change \(H_m\), \(a_m\), \(b\), or \(k\).

novel.justification: Finite stratified Bernoulli source-fusion experiments with randomized source and treatment allocation are standard learnable subexperiments; the paired sign is implemented by two centered subcells within each observed stratum.

assumptions.condition: \(C\) is a measurable, optionally independently randomized map into pairs of closed intervals.

standard.name: Projection of confidence intervals onto the parameter range

definitions.name: Paired-cell observed experiment
definitions.construction: For \(h\in H_m\), under \(P_{m,h}\), \(V\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), \(J\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and \(Z\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{-1,1\}\) are mutually independent; conditionally on \(X\), \(S\) and \(T\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\); and \(B\mid X,S,T\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), where \(p=1/2\) if \(S=1\), \(p=p_0+Zh_{V,J}\) if \(S=0,T=V\), and \(p=7/18\) if \(S=0,T=1-V\). Set \(Y=1/2+B\) and \(P_{m,h}^{n}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n}P_{m,h}\).

definitions.name: Compatible bounded causal completions
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{m,h}=\{Q: \operatorname{Obs}(Q)=P_{m,h},\;Q\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:experimental-randomization},\mathrm{ass:bounded-outcomes},\mathrm{ass:confounding-cap},\mathrm{ass:selection-cap}\}\) for every \(m\ge1\) and \(h\in H_m\).

definitions.name: Jointly honest normalized interval pairs
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_{n,m}=\{C=(C_L,C_U): C\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:interval-map},\mathrm{ass:range-projection},\mathrm{ass:joint-honesty}\}\) for every \(n,m\ge1\) in the normalized experiment.

definitions.name: Jointly calibrated signed-cell-mean interval benchmark
definitions.construction: Set \(\overline h_{v,j}=N_{v,j}^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf1\{V_i=v,J_i=j,S_i=0,T_i=v\}R_i\) when \(N_{v,j}>0\), set \(\overline h_{v,j}=0\) otherwise, and set \(\widehat s_{v,j}=1\) when \(\overline h_{v,j}\ge0\) and \(\widehat s_{v,j}=-1\) otherwise. Define the unprojected endpoint centers \(\overline L_{n,m}=-b+(k/m)\sum_{j=1}^{m}\widehat s_{0,j}\overline h_{0,j}\) and \(\overline U_{n,m}=b-(k/m)\sum_{j=1}^{m}\widehat s_{1,j}\overline h_{1,j}\). Define \(\widehat\psi_{L,i}=8k\sum_{j=1}^{m}\widehat s_{0,j}\mathbf1\{V_i=0,J_i=j,S_i=0,T_i=0\}(R_i-\overline h_{0,j})\), \(\widehat\psi_{U,i}=-8k\sum_{j=1}^{m}\widehat s_{1,j}\mathbf1\{V_i=1,J_i=j,S_i=0,T_i=1\}(R_i-\overline h_{1,j})\), \(\widehat\sigma_L^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat\psi_{L,i}^2\), and \(\widehat\sigma_U^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat\psi_{U,i}^2\). Let \(\kappa_{\delta_0}=\Phi_{\mathrm N}^{-1}((1+\sqrt{1-\delta_0})/2)\). The named procedure is \[C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m}=\left(\Pi_{[-b,-b+ka_m]}\left[\overline L_{n,m}\mathbin{-}\frac{\kappa_{\delta_0}\widehat\sigma_L}{\sqrt n},\overline L_{n,m}\mathbin{+}\frac{\kappa_{\delta_0}\widehat\sigma_L}{\sqrt n}\right],\;\Pi_{[b-ka_m,b]}\left[\overline U_{n,m}\mathbin{-}\frac{\kappa_{\delta_0}\widehat\sigma_U}{\sqrt n},\overline U_{n,m}\mathbin{+}\frac{\kappa_{\delta_0}\widehat\sigma_U}{\sqrt n}\right]\right),\] where \(\Pi_I[A]\) is the image of interval \(A\) under scalar projection onto \(I\).

definitions.name: Mixed tie--boundary profile slice
definitions.construction: For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,m\}\), define \(h^{(r)}\in H_m\) by \(h^{(r)}_{0,j}=0\) for \(j\le r\), \(h^{(r)}_{0,j}=a_m\) for \(j>r\), and \(h^{(r)}_{1,j}=a_m\) for every \(j\). Thus \(T_0(h^{(r)})=(m-r)a_m/m\) and \(T_1(h^{(r)})=a_m\).

definitions.name: Profile-slice composite-test inversion handle
definitions.construction: For a reference \(h\in H_m\), endpoint index \(v\), connected target slice \(B_0\subseteq[0,a_m]\), and degree \(D\ge n\), begin with \[\min_{0\le u_{\omega}\le1}\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_{n,m}}f_h(\omega)u_{\omega}\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_{n,m}}f_g(\omega)u_{\omega}\ge1-\delta_0/4\quad\forall g\in H_m\text{ with }T_v(g)\in B_0.\] On each of the \(2^{2m}\) sign orthants, write \(g\) as the signed version of \(\zeta\in[0,a_m]^{2m}\), triangulate the cube intersected with the two linear slice inequalities, elevate the degree \(n\) count-likelihood polynomial to Bernstein degree \(D\), and impose nonnegativity of every Bernstein coefficient of \(\sum_{\omega}f_g(\omega)u_{\omega}-(1-\delta_0/4)\) on every simplex. This is a conservative linear program with \(\binom{n+32m-1}{32m-1}\) acceptance variables and at most \(2^{2m}\binom{\binom{4m+2}{2m}}{2m+1}\binom{D+2m}{2m}\) coefficient inequalities per target slice, using the vertex bound for a \(2m\)-polytope with \(4m+2\) facet inequalities. Invert nested accepted slices and coordinate the two endpoint tests within the joint level budget. The resulting degree-indexed family is \(\mathfrak H_{n,m}\); the open task includes proving an explicit sufficient degree or a sharper orbit-reduced complexity bound.

definitions.name: Adaptive honest-family handle
definitions.construction: Design \(C_{n,m}^{\star}\) by applying \(\mathfrak H_{n,m}\) on a dimensionless finite grid of likelihood or factorial-polynomial certificates, retaining only candidates whose connected acceptance regions pass simultaneous gap and remainder tests, and taking nested endpoint hulls with the selection error included in the level budget.

definitions.name: Implementation-only outer ATE interval
definitions.construction: Definitional corollary with no theorem-level credit: set \(C_{\mathrm{ATE}}=[\inf C_L,\sup C_U]\). On the joint endpoint-coverage event, this interval contains the entire sharp set \([L_m(h),U_m(h)]\), so joint endpoint honesty supplies the usual outer-set coverage as an implementation consequence.

definitions.name: Implementation-only outcome-scaled pushforward experiment
definitions.construction: Implementation-only pushforward with no theorem-level credit: for each \(d>0\), define \(\mathsf S_d(X,S,T,Y(0),Y(1),Y)=(X,S,T,dY(0),dY(1),dY)\), with the analogous restriction to observed records. Set \(P^{(d)}_{m,h}=(\mathsf S_d)_{\#}P_{m,h}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(d)}_{m,h}=\{(\mathsf S_d)_{\#}Q:Q\in\mathcal M_{m,h}\}\). The observed support is \(\{d/2,3d/2\}\), the potential-outcome support is \([0,2d]\), and the endpoint map is \((dL_m(h),dU_m(h))\). The pushforward leaves \(h\), \(H_m\), \(a_m\), \(b\), \(k\), \(\rho\), and \(\gamma\) unchanged.

definitions.name: Implementation-only pushforward interval decision family
definitions.construction: Implementation-only transformation with no theorem-level credit: for \(C\in\mathcal I_{n,m}\), define \(C^{(d)}(\mathsf S_d(O_1),\ldots,\mathsf S_d(O_n))=dC(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), where multiplication by \(d\) scales both endpoints of both component intervals. Set \(\mathcal I^{(d)}_{n,m}=\{C^{(d)}:C\in\mathcal I_{n,m}\}\), \(R^{(d)}_{n,m}(C^{(d)},h)=\mathbb E_{(P^{(d)}_{m,h})^n}[\operatorname{length}_{\Sigma}(C^{(d)})]\), \(\ell^{(d)}_{n,m}(h)=\inf_{C^{(d)}\in\mathcal I^{(d)}_{n,m}}R^{(d)}_{n,m}(C^{(d)},h)\), and \(\mathfrak A^{(d)}_{n,m}=\inf_{C^{(d)}\in\mathcal I^{(d)}_{n,m}}\sup_{h\in H_m}R^{(d)}_{n,m}(C^{(d)},h)/\ell^{(d)}_{n,m}(h)\), where \(\operatorname{length}_{\Sigma}\) sums component lengths. By the definitions, \(C\mapsto C^{(d)}\) is a bijection onto the displayed image class, joint coverage is unchanged, \(R^{(d)}_{n,m}(C^{(d)},h)=dR_{n,m}(C,h)\), \(\ell^{(d)}_{n,m}(h)=d\ell_{n,m}(h)\), and \(\mathfrak A^{(d)}_{n,m}=\mathfrak A_{n,m}\).

statements.statement: For every \(m\ge1\) and \(h\in H_m\), the class \(\mathcal M_{m,h}\) is nonempty. Over this class, the sharp identified set for \(\mathbb E_Q[Y(1)-Y(0)]\) is exactly \([L_m(h),U_m(h)]\), with \(L_m(h)=-49/495+(11/(80m))\sum_{j=1}^{m}|h_{0,j}|\) and \(U_m(h)=49/495-(11/(80m))\sum_{j=1}^{m}|h_{1,j}|\). Each endpoint is attained by a completion whose missing potential-outcome means lie strictly inside \((0,2)\) in the normalized experiment. The displayed pair is equivalent to the specialization of Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 of LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025 to \(P_{m,h}\), \(\rho=\gamma=1/5\), and support \([0,2]\).
statements.justification: This embeds the statistical experiment in the published data-fusion sensitivity model and verifies that the hard endpoints are causal rather than synthetic functionals.
statements.gap: LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025 proves the general max/min formulas; this theorem specializes them and adds uniform interior endpoint-attaining completions for the paired cube.
statements.consumer: It makes every interval theorem directly interpretable for the Project STAR sensitivity endpoints and the associated implementation.

statements.statement: There are constants \(0<c<C_0<\infty\), depending only on \(\delta_0\) and \(c_0\), such that for every \(n,m\ge1\) and \(h\in H_m\), \[ck\min\{a_m,n^{-1/2}\}\le\ell_{n,m}(h)\le2ka_m.\] In particular, the denominator in \(\mathfrak A_{n,m}\) is strictly positive at every cube face and corner.
statements.justification: Positivity is required before an oracle ratio can be a well-defined decision criterion.
statements.gap: Low1997 provides general coverage-to-length logic, but not the explicit perturbation within this bounded paired Bernoulli cube.
statements.consumer: It validates the simultaneous adaptation factor used to compare implementable endpoint procedures.

statements.statement: The capped cell estimator satisfies, uniformly over every \(m\ge1\) and \(h\in H_m\), \[\frac1{2m}\sum_{v=0}^{1}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\mathbb E_{P_{m,h}^{n}}[(\widehat h_{v,j}-h_{v,j})^2]\le C_0\min\{a_m^2,m/(n+1)\}\le C_0n^{-2/3}.\] Moreover, with probability at least \(1-\eta\), \[\max_{v,j}|\widehat h_{v,j}-h_{v,j}|\le C_0\min\left\{a_m,\sqrt{m\log(6m/\eta)/n}\right\}.\] Both bounds include empty cells and follow from the displayed experiment rather than a maintained nuisance-rate assumption.
statements.justification: The fixed union must be shown learnable without importing an oracle nuisance rate.
statements.gap: The data-fusion papers allow flexible nuisance estimation but do not derive a uniform finite-union empty-cell bound for this experiment.
statements.consumer: It supplies explicit remainder inputs for any smooth or factorial candidate inside the honest adaptive family.

statements.statement: At the exact tie \(h=0\), uniformly for every \(n,m\ge1\), \[\ell_{n,m}(0)\asymp k\min\{a_m,m^{1/4}/\sqrt n\},\] with constants depending only on \(\delta_0\) and \(c_0\). The lower bound is obtained from a balanced-sign composite mixture and the upper bound from an explicit capped quadratic \(U\)-statistic interval that remains valid with empty cells.
statements.justification: The tie is the main nonregular benchmark and shows why zero smoothing bias does not imply zero statistical uncertainty.
statements.gap: CaiLow2011 gives an absolute-functional point-risk lower bound, not a finite-sample honest connected-interval oracle under binomial occupancy.
statements.consumer: It quantifies the uncertainty hidden by fixed-temperature standard errors at crossover cells.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C_0<\infty\), depending only on \(\delta_0\) and \(c_0\), such that whenever \(n\le\sqrt m/(20a_m^2)\), uniformly for all \(h\in H_m\), \[ck\{2a_m-T_0(h)-T_1(h)+\min(a_m,n^{-1/2})\}\le\ell_{n,m}(h)\le C_0k\{2a_m-T_0(h)-T_1(h)+\min(a_m,n^{-1/2})\}.\] The lower bound uses a mean-preserving corner mixture at the reference profile, and the upper bound uses a fixed-sign honest interval admissible in the pointwise oracle.
statements.justification: This supplies a verified full-profile base regime and isolates the exact boundary where corner mixtures cease to be informative.
statements.gap: Neither local-modulus theory for linear functionals nor absolute-functional point estimation yields this reference-specific deficit formula.
statements.consumer: It calibrates how endpoint precision changes from ties to full-corner separation in small stratified fusion samples.

statements.statement: Whenever \(n\le\sqrt m/(20a_m^2)\), \[\mathfrak A_{n,m}\asymp\max\{1,a_m\sqrt n\}.\] A single full-range interval pair attains the upper bound, and a mean-preserving full-corner mixture gives the matching lower bound over all measurable, optionally randomized members of \(\mathcal I_{n,m}\). At the upper boundary of this regime the factor has order \(m^{1/4}\).
statements.justification: The result proves that simultaneous adaptation can be polynomially costly even though every fixed profile has an honest oracle procedure.
statements.gap: CaiLow2004 organizes adaptation across linear-functional classes; it does not establish this nonlinear full-profile oracle ratio or the \(m^{1/4}\) obstruction.
statements.consumer: It warns applied users that one fixed smooth-bound interval cannot be judged by pointwise approximation error alone.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{n,m}\), determine an explicit expression or certified finite-dimensional computation \(\Phi_{n,m}(h)\) and an explicit order \(q_{n,m}\), including every necessary logarithmic factor, such that uniformly over all \(n,m\ge1\) and \(h\in H_m\), \[c\Phi_{n,m}(h)\le\ell_{n,m}(h)\le C_0\Phi_{n,m}(h),\qquad c q_{n,m}\le\mathfrak A_{n,m}\le C_0 q_{n,m}.\] Derive one implementable family \(C_{n,m}^{\star}\in\mathcal I_{n,m}\), depending on the data and \(m\) but not on \(h\), with \[\sup_{h\in H_m}R_{n,m}(C_{n,m}^{\star},h)/\ell_{n,m}(h)\le C_0q_{n,m},\] and prove the matching lower bound over every \(C\in\mathcal I_{n,m}\). The characterization must remain valid at exact ties, heterogeneous near ties, cube boundaries, and separated profiles, and it must specialize to \(\mathrm{thm:exact-tie-oracle}\) and \(\mathrm{thm:low-information-profile}\). As an explicit high-information falsification slice, whenever \(na_m^2/m\ge C_0\log(2m)\), determine whether the mixed profiles in \(\mathrm{def:high-information-slice}\) satisfy, uniformly in \(0\le r\le m\), \[\Phi_{n,m}(h^{(r)})\asymp k\left\{\min\left(\frac{ra_m}{m},\frac{r^{3/4}}{\sqrt{mn}}\right)+\sqrt{\frac{m-r}{mn}}+\frac1{\sqrt n}\right\}.\] A valid solution must either prove this display or replace it with a contradicted profile and the correct constant-order expression. It must also evaluate the Bernstein-certified likelihood program in \(\mathrm{def:testing-handle}\): prove that the explicit choice \(D=\lceil n+C_0m\log(2m)\rceil\) attains the slice profile up to constants, or give a counterexample and an explicit sufficient degree or orbit-reduced complexity bound.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it asks for the local honest oracle, the exact simultaneous adaptation price, one attaining finite-sample procedure, and the all-procedure converse.
statements.gap: CaiLowXia2013 treats a local oracle in ordered shape models, CaiLow2011 treats point risk for a Gaussian absolute functional, and LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025 uses fixed smoothing; none contains this full paired-binomial frontier.
statements.consumer: The result determines when the Project STAR max/min sensitivity endpoints can be reported precisely and when tie uncertainty necessarily dominates smooth-bound standard errors.

statements.statement: Fix \(m\ge1\) and \(0<\xi\le a_m\), and let \(n\to\infty\). Uniformly over \(h\in H_m(\xi)\), the local honest oracle has the regular order \[\ell_{n,m}(h)\asymp_{m,\xi,\delta_0}n^{-1/2},\qquad \Phi_{n,m}(h)\asymp_{m,\xi,\delta_0}n^{-1/2}.\] The named signed-cell-mean procedure in \(\mathrm{def:signed-cell-mean-interval}\) has jointly calibrated limiting coverage \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{h\in H_m(\xi)}P_{m,h}^{n}\{L_m(h)\in(C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m})_L,\ U_m(h)\in(C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m})_U\}\ge1-\delta_0.\] An attaining full-profile family can be chosen so that \[\sup_{h\in H_m(\xi)}\frac{R_{n,m}(C_{n,m}^{\star},h)}{\ell_{n,m}(h)}=O_{m,\xi,\delta_0}(1).\] Here first-order equivalence means endpoint-center equivalence only: for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\sup_{h\in H_m(\xi)}P_{m,h}^{n}\!\left(\sqrt n\left[\left|\operatorname{mid}((C_{n,m}^{\star})_L)-\operatorname{mid}((C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m})_L)\right|+\left|\operatorname{mid}((C_{n,m}^{\star})_U)-\operatorname{mid}((C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m})_U)\right|\right]>\varepsilon\right)\longrightarrow0.\] No expected-length-ratio or Hausdorff equivalence is asserted.
statements.justification: This fixed-dimension limit is the precise regular special-case reduction and a falsification check for any claimed all-regime frontier.
statements.gap: Fixed-margin influence-function results give a regular endpoint center, but they do not identify the local honest oracle or prove a bounded full-profile oracle ratio on the separated domain.
statements.consumer: It recovers conventional efficient endpoint inference in applications whose active max/min operations are well separated.

sampling_model.design: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the fully specified finite paired-cell law \(P_{m,h}\), and the label \(m\) is observed.
sampling_model.units: Each normalized unit has \(X=(m,V,J,Z)\), source \(S\), treatment \(T\), observed outcome \(Y=1/2+B\in\{1/2,3/2\}\), and potential outcomes supported on \([0,2]\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditionally on \(X\), \(S\) and \(T\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\); in the experimental source, treatment is randomized.
sampling_model.overlap: Every design, source, and treatment probability equals \(1/2\), and all Bernoulli outcome probabilities are uniformly inside \((0,1)\) for \(h\in H_m\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the \(2m\) informative gaps are unknown. They are learned globally from capped cell means with an explicit empty-cell rule. On fixed-dimensional separated profiles, the named regular benchmark uses uncapped cell means, estimated signs, empirical influence-score variances, and the joint critical value \(\kappa_{\delta_0}\). Any smooth or polynomial adaptive candidate must charge its own remainder and selection uncertainty.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 derive sharp max/min sensitivity endpoints, while Section 5 replaces them by fixed-temperature Boltzmann approximations for influence-function inference.
The paper defines minimum expected length at a fixed function among globally honest intervals and attains its local-modulus benchmark for monotone and convex regression.
The paper proves the sharp minimax mean-squared-error frontier for an average absolute Gaussian mean by composite priors and Hermite-polynomial estimators.
The paper characterizes adaptive honest confidence intervals for linear functionals through between-class and ordered moduli.
The paper establishes lower bounds on pointwise expected interval length under uniform coverage and shows that honest adaptation can fail.
Section 5.4 gives a fixed-smoothing Wald interval and leaves data-driven tuning for the shortest confidence interval open.
Theorem 2 and Corollary D.1 establish asymptotic inference for deterministic entropic regularization under margin and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper proves minimax point-estimation rates for nonsmooth discrete-distribution functionals using best-polynomial approximation and unbiased discrete moments.
The paper constructs one-at-a-time functional intervals by constrained likelihood-ratio inversion in linear Gaussian inverse problems.

tldr: Sharp data-fusion sensitivity endpoints are averages of absolute paired-cell gaps, so exact and near ties create a confidence problem that fixed smoothing does not resolve. The project computes the local minimum expected summed length of jointly honest endpoint intervals throughout the full heterogeneous gap cube, determines the least multiplicative price paid by one profile-independent procedure, and constructs a finite-sample honest family attaining that price. Exact-tie and low-information results provide the tractable reductions; a mixed tie--boundary slice and a Bernstein-certified likelihood program make the open higher-information full-profile frontier explicitly falsifiable, including every logarithmic factor.

project_justification.gap: Published data-fusion work identifies the max/min endpoints and uses fixed smoothing, while confidence adaptation theory concerns linear or ordered functionals and absolute-functional theory concerns point risk. None evaluates the connected-interval local oracle and simultaneous adaptation cost for the paired binomial endpoint experiment.
project_justification.niche: The fixed learnable subclass isolates the statistical cost of ties without nuisance ambiguity, retains both causal endpoints and joint coverage, and exposes heterogeneous profiles that a scalar margin condition removes.
project_justification.fill: The project combines exact paired-binomial composite tests, moment-matched alternatives, a finite Bernstein-certified likelihood hierarchy with an explicit size bound, and nested inversion to give an explicit oracle profile, a sharp oracle ratio, and one implementable honest endpoint family.

related_work: ColnetMayerEtAl2024 surveys the broader trial--observational fusion literature without a tie-adaptive endpoint-confidence result. LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025 supplies the causal sensitivity endpoints and the applied Project STAR motivation; its fixed-temperature inference is an input, not a theorem-level target. CaiLowXia2013 supplies the closest local expected-length criterion, but its ordered shape-constrained Gaussian geometry does not cover a nonlinear absolute average. CaiLow2011 supplies the composite-prior and polynomial tools for the absolute-value cusp, but only for minimax point estimation. CaiLow2004 and Low1997 organize honest adaptation for linear functionals and furnish coverage-to-testing logic. LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025 explicitly leaves shortest-interval smoothing selection open, while BenMichael2025 handles deterministic growing regularization under margin conditions. JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 motivates factorial moments for sparse cells, and BatllePatilStanleyOwhadiKuusela2024 motivates finite-sample test inversion but is confined to constrained linear Gaussian inverse problems.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact-tie statement covers every \(n,m\), whereas the displayed full-profile formula is asserted only when \(n\le\sqrt m/(20a_m^2)\). Beyond this regime, the corner mixture is statistically distinguishable and the deficit formula cannot be extrapolated. The Bernstein-certified likelihood hierarchy supplies explicit variables, constraints, and a per-slice size bound, but it is not itself a frontier: the solver must establish a sufficient certificate degree, evaluate the mixed tie--boundary slice, control connected-hull length, and prove an implementable uniform upper bound.
honest_scope: All endpoint, compatibility, oracle, and adaptation claims are stated for the normalized experiment with observed outcomes in \(\{1/2,3/2\}\) and potential outcomes in \([0,2]\). Arbitrary outcome units and the conventional outer ATE interval appear only as implementation-level definitional consequences and receive no theorem-level credit; the pushforward does not alter \(h\), \(H_m\), \(a_m\), \(b\), or \(k\). The mathematical kernel concerns the displayed fixed union of paired-cell Bernoulli experiments and joint confidence intervals for its two sharp endpoints; it does not claim unrestricted nonparametric data-fusion inference. The exact-tie, low-information, causal-completion, positivity, and nuisance-learning statements are traction that must be independently proved. The higher-information profile \(\Phi_{n,m}(h)\), the sharp factor \(q_{n,m}\), the mixed tie--boundary slice, and the attaining interval family remain open. For fixed \(m\) and \(\xi\), the separated-profile check uses the explicitly centered and jointly calibrated procedure \(C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m}\), requires an \(n^{-1/2}\) oracle and a bounded oracle ratio, and asserts endpoint-center equivalence only. At \(h=0\), the profile must collapse to \(k\min\{a_m,m^{1/4}/\sqrt n\}\).

seed_details.anchor: LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025, Lemma 1, Theorem 1, Section 5, and Section 7; CaiLowXia2013, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--4; CaiLow2011, Theorems 1--3 and Sections 3--5.
seed_details.opportunity: Compute the local minimum expected summed length and the least simultaneous adaptation factor for the two sharp paired-cell endpoints over the entire heterogeneous cube.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the ordered local-modulus step in Cai, Low, and Xia by profile-indexed composite tests in the exact paired Bernoulli experiment; unlike the Gaussian point-risk argument of Cai and Low, coverage must be converted directly into expected connected-interval length.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for honest confidence intervals for average absolute normal means, nonlinear-functional minimum expected length, and local honest oracle adaptation returned linear-functional, shape-constrained, confidence-ball, and dissertation results, but no theorem for a joint binomial absolute-average endpoint pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from CaiLowXia2013 because their local modulus already characterizes minimum expected length at every parameter.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their target is point evaluation over ordered monotone or convex cones in Gaussian white noise; the present functional is nonlinear, the parameter cube is unordered, the sampling experiment has random binomial occupancy, and the target is a jointly honest pair with a second-stage all-profile oracle ratio.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The focal objects are explicit decision quantities, the fixed experiment is nondegenerate, and the kernel requires both an attainable construction and an all-procedure converse rather than an undefined modulus.

seed_details.anchor: LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025, Section 5.4; LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025, Section 5.1; BenMichael2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary D.1.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a finite-sample honest selector over dimensionless smoothing temperatures, polynomial degrees, and truncation scales whose expected summed endpoint length tracks the best certified candidate at each full gap profile.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace deterministic regularization in Ben-Michael by sample-split gap certification and simultaneous bias-remainder envelopes; every candidate must charge its approximation error, temperature times squared nuisance error, occupancy error, and selection error.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest papers give a fixed-temperature Wald interval, deterministic growing regularization under a margin condition, or bias-aware bandwidth choice for linear functionals; none supplies exact-tie finite-sample selection for both endpoints.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Lepski selection once each temperature has a confidence interval.
seed_details.rebuttal: At a tie, candidate biases are ordered but their data-dependent remainder bounds and false separation declarations are not; coverage after selecting a nonlinear candidate is the missing theorem, not a direct Lepski corollary.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is not a fixed-temperature central limit theorem: it requires finite-sample honesty and an expected-length oracle inequality including the selection charge.

seed_details.anchor: CaiLow2011, Sections 3--5; JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015, Sections III--IV; BatllePatilStanleyOwhadiKuusela2024, Theorem 2.1 and Section 3.
seed_details.opportunity: Develop exact or conservative binomial test inversion based on factorial-polynomial certificates for both absolute-average endpoints with empty and low-count cells.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Hermite moments with unbiased products under the multinomial count experiment and prove exponential or calibrated polynomial tails before inverting the composite tests into connected intervals.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found factorial-polynomial minimax point estimation and constrained Gaussian likelihood-ratio inversion, but no finite-sample honest confidence-length theorem combining random cell occupancy, nonlinear absolute averages, and joint endpoint coverage.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 by adding a concentration radius to their factorial estimator.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their risk proof neither calibrates a selected high-degree statistic uniformly nor controls connected confidence length; this exact tail gap caused the closest prior proposal to be downgraded.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A transferred mean-squared-error rate is expressly insufficient; direct test inversion and expected-length analysis are part of the seed.

seed_details.anchor: LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025, Theorem 1; BatllePatilStanleyOwhadiKuusela2024, Theorem 2.1 and Section 3.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize whether coupled inversion lowers expected summed marginal length relative to separate or Bonferroni calibration for the two nonlinear endpoints.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace one-functional likelihood-ratio inversion by a bivariate acceptance-region problem under multinomial occupancy and optimize the allocation of type-I error as a function of the two profiles.
seed_details.destination_search: The available simultaneous constrained-inversion work concerns multiple linear functionals and region volume, not two nonlinear projections under expected summed interval length.
seed_details.red_team: The two endpoint coordinates are parameter-separated, so Bonferroni is automatically optimal up to constants.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their counts share a multinomial allocation and the objective is expected summed projected length; whether dependence can improve constants or orders is a nontrivial testing question, although it is narrower than the selected frontier.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names the joint calibration map and an optimization criterion, but its likely constant-only gain caps its ambition.

seed_details.anchor: LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025, Theorem 2 and Section 5.2; BenMichael2025, Theorem 2.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive the facewise semiparametric efficiency bound when all relevant gaps are separated and characterize the smallest honest transition envelope that remains valid as selected gaps approach zero.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Start from the smooth influence function on a fixed sign face, then replace the fixed-face delta method by a uniform local experiment that includes sign changes at the \(n^{-1/2}\) scale.
seed_details.destination_search: Existing efficiency calculations apply to a smooth approximation or impose a margin condition; no located result joins the efficient separated law to a tie-inclusive finite-sample envelope in this paired experiment.
seed_details.red_team: The separated-face efficiency bound is a routine delta-method calculation.
seed_details.rebuttal: That calculation is only the benchmark; the nonroutine content is the least honest transition cost and its attainment uniformly through the exceptional face.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposal would fail if it stopped at the facewise influence function; the transition envelope is the named kernel.

seed_details.opportunity: Derive the non-Gaussian or Gaussian transition limit of an explicit factorial-polynomial endpoint estimator when informative cell occupancy moves from sparse to dense.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed-variance Gaussian-chaos expansion by a Poissonized multinomial Hoeffding decomposition and identify which polynomial orders survive at \(n/(8m)\) of constant order.
seed_details.destination_search: Located work provides point-risk bounds but not a uniform distributional approximation or studentized endpoint law across the random-occupancy transition.
seed_details.red_team: A Poisson central limit theorem yields the answer after poissonization.
seed_details.rebuttal: At the cusp, increasing polynomial degree and empty cells create a changing degenerate chaos, so neither a scalar Poisson CLT nor routine de-poissonization identifies the limit.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a genuine limit-law lane rather than another minimax converse, but it does not alone deliver honest endpoint length.

seed_details.anchor: BenMichael2025, Section 2.2 and Theorem 3; LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025, Theorem 1.
seed_details.opportunity: Choose a treatment rule using lower data-fusion welfare endpoints and derive regret to the best robust rule with a penalty determined by honest endpoint uncertainty.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace plug-in conditional-LP values in empirical welfare maximization by lower confidence scores whose penalty reflects paired-cell tie uncertainty.
seed_details.destination_search: Ben-Michael treats partially identified policy value with regularized estimation, while the located data-fusion paper does not give an honest tie-adaptive policy-regret frontier.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely the endpoint confidence interval inserted into standard empirical welfare maximization.
seed_details.rebuttal: A matching regret result would require optimizing how confidence penalties vary across cells and proving a lower bound coupling policy disagreement with endpoint testing; nevertheless it changes the focal consumer and is not selected here.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The loss is welfare regret and the decision rule is first class, so this is a genuine M16 lane; it is set aside because the brief requires endpoint intervals as the primary output.

seed_details.anchor: Low1997, Theorems 1--2; CaiLow2004, Theorems 1--4; CaiLowXia2013, Theorem 1.
seed_details.opportunity: Define and compute a directed composite-testing modulus for the nonlinear endpoint map, then characterize exactly when it equals the local honest expected-length oracle.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the linear-functional ordered modulus by a directed distance between profile slices of the paired Bernoulli experiment and prove both the coverage-to-testing and testing-to-connected-interval directions.
seed_details.destination_search: General modulus theory located in the scan is restricted to linear functionals or ordered shape classes; no exact nonlinear paired-slice equivalence was found.
seed_details.red_team: This only renames the infimum over confidence procedures as a modulus.
seed_details.rebuttal: The seed is credible only if the modulus is reduced to the finite count-space constraints and proved attainable by connected intervals; an undefined variational object is explicitly excluded.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The evaluable finite-dimensional reduction is mandatory, preventing the computable-map-absent failure.

seed_details.anchor: LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025, Lemma 1 and the paired max/min structure in Theorem 1.
seed_details.opportunity: Invert sign-flip randomization tests in the observed \(Z\)-pairs to obtain exact endpoint confidence intervals.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Attempt to treat \(Z\mapsto-Z\) as a finite symmetry group and invert orbit tests for the magnitude profile.
seed_details.destination_search: The required orbit invariance fails away from \(h=0\): the conditional Bernoulli law changes under a sign flip unless the unknown parameter is transformed with the data.
seed_details.red_team: The alleged randomization symmetry holds only at the exact-tie null and cannot cover the full cube.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; exact binomial likelihood inversion remains available, but it is not an M17 symmetry argument.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The required M17 group action is absent, so this lane is documented as a named search obstruction and dropped.

threads: ColnetMayerEtAl2024 surveys trial--observational fusion, while LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025 supplies the sharp max/min endpoints and fixed-temperature influence-function inference; Lanners et al.'s Section 7 identifies small-sample instability near crossover points.
CaiLowXia2013 supplies the pointwise minimum-expected-length benchmark and multiscale construction, but only for point evaluation over monotone or convex Gaussian models.
CaiLow2011 supplies moment-matched fuzzy priors and best-polynomial estimation for an average absolute Gaussian mean, but only under point-estimation risk.
CaiLow2004 and Low1997 supply coverage-to-length and adaptation lower-bound principles for linear functionals; their ordered moduli do not evaluate the nonlinear paired-cell experiment.
literature_map.settled: The causal endpoint formulas, fixed-temperature smooth inference, general linear-functional adaptation principles, and minimax point estimation of an absolute Gaussian mean are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No located theorem computes the local honest connected-interval oracle and the smallest one-procedure oracle ratio for two random-cell binomial absolute averages.
literature_map.exemplars_used: Writing follows LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025 from complementary trial and observational failures to sharp bounds and then tie instability. The proof handle adapts the local testing logic of CaiLowXia2013 and the moment-matched mixtures of CaiLow2011.

threads: LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025, Section 5.4, explicitly leaves data-driven shortest-interval smoothing selection open.
BenMichael2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary D.1, permits deterministic growing regularization and records the regularization, nuisance, and approximation remainders under margin control.
ArmstrongKolesar2020 optimizes honest bias-aware confidence length for linear-functional estimators, not nonlinear post-selection at exact ties.
LuedtkeVanderLaan2016 stabilizes inference for an optimal value at exceptional laws, without a local expected-length oracle.
literature_map.settled: Candidate-wise bias-aware intervals and deterministic smoothing expansions are available.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: Honest data-driven choice over nonlinear candidates while retaining exact ties and charging selection uncertainty remains unoccupied in the searched sources.
literature_map.exemplars_used: The open tuning statement of Levis et al. determines the motivation; Ben-Michael supplies the remainder accounting that any selected smooth candidate must retain.

threads: CaiLow2011 constructs sharp Hermite-polynomial point estimators and moment-matched Gaussian-mixture lower bounds.
JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 separates smooth and nonsmooth regimes and lifts best polynomials with unbiased discrete moments.
BatllePatilStanleyOwhadiKuusela2024 characterizes constrained likelihood-ratio inversion for linear Gaussian inverse problems and explicitly leaves nonlinear non-Gaussian extensions open.
The prior proposal \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_honest\_inference\_frontier}\) was downgraded because its selected factorial statistic lacked a direct tail certificate.
literature_map.settled: Polynomial point-risk control and Gaussian constrained test inversion are settled separately.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: Their combination does not yet give finite-sample joint honesty, connected intervals, or matched local expected length under random binomial occupancy.
literature_map.exemplars_used: The factorial-polynomial split is adapted from Jiao et al.; the confidence construction starts from Batlle et al.'s test-inversion distinction between numerical optimization and statistical coverage.
